description: The new integer flag exposes window widths that cannot supply a next-token target.
trigger: Invoke standalone `eval/ppl.py` with `--length 1`, successful model initialization, and more than one encoded corpus token. Zero and negative widths are also accepted by the parser without semantic validation.
expected_behavior: Reject widths below two before model work, since scoring requires a token and its successor.
actual_behavior: A one-token row reaches scoring with both prediction and target slices empty. If tensor operations succeed, the target count remains zero and the mean divides by zero. Zero and negative widths likewise reach slicing instead of getting an argument error; their downstream failures were not tested.

verification.description: The slice calculation gave 100 one-token windows and zero target positions.
verification.limits: The check did not run the tensor or model operations that precede the division.

verification.description: The index check produced one row and zero next-token targets for a 10-token input and length one.
verification.limits: No backend was run; a backend may fail before the mean calculation.

introductions.rationale: The parser accepts arbitrary integers and forwards the selected width to slicing and scoring without enforcing the two-token minimum.

finding.description: The CLI admits a one-token window that cannot contribute to next-token perplexity.
finding.trigger: Run with `--length 1`, enough corpus tokens to produce a row, and a backend that completes the forward and empty-target scoring operations.
finding.expected_behavior: Reject a window length below two or report that there are no scorable targets.
finding.actual_behavior: Target slices are empty, the count stays zero, and `main` divides by zero if it reaches the mean calculation. The copied native scoring loop has the same unchecked denominator.

affected_revisions.limits: Source and scalar slice check only. Tensor operations with zero targets and the behavior for zero or negative widths were not run. Source and scalar slice checks for the native and Transformers paths. No backend or tensor operations were run, and earlier failures remain possible.
